title: ALP per-family pin-mux capability table (metadata/pinmux/<family>.yaml) v1
description: Structured, queryable projection of a SoM family's pin-mux: each E1M edge pad maps to the silicon function/peripheral that backs it and the on-module silicon that owns it.  GENERATED from metadata/e1m_modules/<family>/*.tsv by scripts/gen_pinmux_capability.py and gated byte-in-sync (the TSVs remain the single source).  A CLI/IDE queries this table instead of parsing the heterogeneous raw TSVs.  Pad exclusivity (no silicon pad backing two E1M functions) is enforced separately by scripts/check_pin_conflicts.py.

allOf.description: `core` is a Renesas-only fact: its value set (a55 / m33) names RZ/V2N cores, and `renesas` is the only currently-multi-core owner.  A gd32-owned or cc3501e-owned row carrying a `core` is an attribution error, not a stricter fact -- the GD32 supervisor MCU's own pads (GD32_SPI.SCLK/PA9, .MOSI/PB15, .MISO/PA10, .CS0/PA8) share the *peripheral* name with the four CM33-driven RZ/V2N pads on the other end of the same link, so a core-ownership entry keyed to the wrong end of an inter-chip link lands here.  Rejecting it in the schema means the generator refuses to WRITE such a table (it validates before writing) rather than emitting an authoritative-looking file that is wrong about four pads.  When another multi-core owner is attributed (alif: M55-HE / M55-HP), widen `core`'s enum and this `const` together.

e1m_pad.description: E1M edge-connector ball name.  The literal "TBD" when the family's source TSVs are pad-first peripheral maps that don't carry the edge ball (V2N) -- never invented.

e1m_function.description: E1M-standard function name.  The literal "TBD" when the source row is an on-module / inter-chip net that doesn't surface at the E1M connector, or when the source TSV doesn't state the E1M function.

owner.description: On-module silicon that drives the pad.  Per-family legal values: aen -> alif | cc3501e; v2n -> renesas | gd32.

core.description: Which AMP core on the `owner` silicon drives the pad, for owners whose silicon is itself multi-core (renesas: A55 Linux vs CM33 Zephyr).  Present ONLY for pads with silicon-verified evidence (devicetree pinctrl claim, runtime alp_gpio_* claim, or an in-tree errata/patch) -- absent means "not attributed", never "shared" or "a55 by elimination".  Sourced from metadata/e1m_modules/<family>/core-ownership.yaml, not invented by the generator.

silicon_peripheral.description: Silicon peripheral/function backing the pad.  Empty when the pad is plain GPIO (no dedicated peripheral mux) -- faithful to the source TSV's empty cell.
